Hi Rachel — thanks for flagging this and for sending the NDA. Appreciate the redaction note.

High level: Gartner usually records the briefing for internal analyst use (audio + transcript). Recording access is limited to Gartner analysts and their research team; retention policies vary by Gartner but they told us they keep recordings for up to 12 months for quality and follow-up. We always ask customers to approve recording/quote usage in writing before the session.

On scope: we will ensure the conversation focuses on architecture, inference economics, and deployment experience (latency/cost improvements, rollout notes). We explicitly exclude PHI and any raw customer data — we will prepare a short prep deck with suggested talking points and redaction guidance so you can pre-approve.

Marissa, Ben — looping you in to confirm our standard consent wording and whether Legal needs to sign off on Vetta's NDA or if we can use our consent form to accept the limitations.

Connor —

Thanks for the ping. Per our reference program playbook:
- We ask customers to sign our Reference Consent (link below) which covers recording, attribution, and quote usage. If a customer provides their own NDA, Legal needs to do a quick review (typically 24–48 hours).
- Prep: we send a 1-page briefing doc + a 5-slide prep-deck (no sensitive data) for pre-approval.
- Logistics: we recommend a 30–45 minute call; Gartner likes closed Q&A at the end and a brief demo or screenshots only if pre-cleared.

Links: https://drive.google.com/redwood/reference-consent (template), prep-deck stub attached.

Ben — please confirm if we should accept Vetta's NDA as-is or ask Legal to redline. If Legal signs, include the signed copy in the Drive folder.
